stories.statLabel: Iranian demands to end the war
stories.headline: Trump says new Iran strikes unlikely as peace talks continue
body: Trump says renewed strikes on Iran are unlikely while talks to end the war make progress.
Iran reported more US strikes on Qeshm island overnight, and insists its seven demands stand.
Oil prices dipped after Brent fell 17% last week.
stories.vc: A real deal would ease oil prices, a big relief for India's import bill.

stories.statLabel: minimum wage rise, now from 1 Dec
stories.headline: France brings forward its minimum wage rise to calm protests
body: France will raise its minimum wage by 1.6% from 1 December, a month earlier than planned.
That lifts it by €24 to about €1,502 a month.
Unions say it's not enough after weeks of protests over living costs.
stories.joke: €24 a month: enough for a baguette a day, roughly.
stories.vc: Wage concessions in France could spread pay pressure across Europe and keep rates higher.

stories.headline: South Africa detains nine men suspected of heading to fight for Russia
body: South African police arrested nine foreign nationals they suspect were going to fight in Russia's war on Ukraine.
The men, aged 20 to 26, were stopped at Johannesburg's airport and a nearby hotel.
Reports say many Africans have been tricked into joining Russia's forces.
stories.vc: Recruitment scams exploit young job seekers, a sign of how scarce work is for them.

stories.headline: Foreign investors are back, buying ₹45,960 crore of Indian shares
body: Foreign investors bought a net ₹45,960 crore of Indian shares in the week to 6 November.
That more than reversed October's ₹45,162 crore of selling.
The Nifty rose 8.6% over the period; it closed near 25,045 on Monday.
stories.joke: Foreign money: back from its holiday, wallet open.
stories.vc: Returning foreign money supports the rupee and helps companies raise capital.

stories.statLabel: ONGC Videsh stake in San Cristobal
stories.headline: ONGC expects to run Venezuelan oil projects within 6 months
body: ONGC Videsh is in advanced talks to take over running two Venezuelan oil projects.
It owns 40% of San Cristobal, alongside Venezuela's state oil company.
ONGC says it has the needed approvals, including US sanctions clearance.
stories.vc: Running fields abroad gives India more control over its oil supply.

stories.headline: Centre orders traders to declare rice stocks as prices rise
body: The Centre ordered rice traders, retailers and millers across India to declare their stocks weekly.
Rice prices are rising after a weak and uneven monsoon.
Five southern states may set stock limits to stop hoarding.
stories.joke: Rice: now tracked more closely than your parcel.
stories.vc: Stock limits can cool prices but squeeze traders' margins.

stories.headline: Anthropic buys $3.4B of gas turbines to power its AI
body: Anthropic is spending $3.4 billion on Caterpillar natural gas generators, the FT reports.
They can produce up to 1.7 gigawatts of power.
The company usually rents computing, but power has become scarce.
stories.joke: Step one: build smart AI. Step two: buy a power plant.
stories.vc: AI labs owning power assets shows how energy is becoming the main bottleneck for AI.

stories.headline: Geothermal firm Fervo now has about $12B in orders
body: Fervo says it now has $11.9 billion of contracted revenue, up from $7.2 billion last quarter.
It is building a 396-megawatt plant for Google in Utah.
Its first 100-megawatt plant joined the grid this year.
stories.joke: Turns out the earth's basement has plenty of power.
stories.vc: AI's hunger for steady power is making geothermal an investable business.

stories.headline: AI hardware-testing startup Nominal triples value to $3B
body: Nominal raised a $240 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation, led by Lightspeed.
Its AI platform helps test complex hardware like aircraft and reactors.
It has 80 customers, including defence firm Anduril.
stories.joke: Tripling in 8 months: the hardware is hard, the valuation isn't.
stories.vc: Defence and industrial AI is drawing some of the year's fastest valuation jumps.

stories.headline: Huang scandal puts Nvidia's China plans under scrutiny
body: Jensen Huang's admitted affair with an alleged Chinese spy is complicating his push to sell AI chips to China.
Nvidia's independent directors are investigating, and Congress wants answers.
Huang also pulled out of a speaking event.
stories.vc: China access matters for Nvidia's growth; tighter export rules would hit sales.

stories.headline: Uber launches parking bookings after buying SpotHero
body: Uber now lets users book and pay for parking in major US cities.
It uses SpotHero's network of 13,000 garages and lots in 400+ cities.
Later, the spots could hold robotaxis between rides.
stories.joke: Uber found a way to profit even when you don't take an Uber.
stories.vc: Parking networks could become key real estate for robotaxi fleets.

stories.headline: Russell Brand jailed for over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
body: A London judge sentenced Russell Brand to 10 years and six months in prison.
He was found guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault involving four women.
Brand had denied all the charges.
stories.vc: Big convictions push media firms to act faster on harassment complaints.

stories.headline: Woman IPS officer manhandled over Diwali crackers in Cuttack
body: Odisha police arrested four people for allegedly manhandling IPS officer Ananya Awasthi in Cuttack.
She had stopped residents bursting crackers past the allowed time on Diwali night.
Firecrackers were allowed only from 7 to 9 pm.
stories.vc: Attacks on women officers on duty add to calls for better protection in policing.

stories.headline: Black women's long fight restores voting rights in Virginia
body: Virginians voted to end a Jim Crow-era law that blocked people with felony convictions from voting.
The change followed a decades-long effort led by Black women like Sheba Williams.
Williams lost her vote for nine years; her mother lost hers for 24.
stories.vc: Restoring votes to ex-offenders can help them return to work and civic life.

stories.headline: Warangal's super speciality hospital nears full opening
body: Telangana's health minister told officials to speed up final works at the Warangal Super Speciality Hospital.
Outpatient services were set to start on 20 October.
The chief minister is expected to open the full hospital after 15 December.
stories.vc: A big public hospital in Warangal cuts trips to Hyderabad for specialist care.

stories.headline: Telangana to finish 25 new hospital buildings by March 2027
body: Telangana says it will complete 25 hospital buildings under its secondary health care department by March 2027.
Nine are already finished.
The minister reviewed progress in Hyderabad on Monday.
stories.vc: More district-level hospitals reduce crowding at big city hospitals.

stories.headline: Haryana adds 19 newborn ventilators and mother-baby care units
body: Haryana will add 19 neonatal ventilators to its 54, across 29 newborn care units, for about ₹7 crore.
It is also upgrading units so mothers can stay with their sick babies.
The aim is better emergency care for newborns.
stories.vc: Better newborn units cut infant deaths, one of the best-value health investments.

stories.headline: Oscar Piastri splits with manager Mark Webber
body: Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have ended their management deal by mutual agreement.
Webber had managed him since 2019 and helped move him from Alpine to McLaren.
Piastri has 9 wins and 6 poles in 88 starts.
stories.joke: Even the best partnerships need a pit stop.
stories.vc: A new manager could reshape Piastri's sponsorship and future contract talks.
